subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which of these is a greenhouse gas?
questions.explain: Methane is a greenhouse gas, along with carbon dioxide and water vapour.

questions.q: As the early oceans formed, water vapour in the atmosphere:
questions.explain: As the Earth cooled, water vapour condensed to form the oceans.

questions.q: Carbon from the early atmosphere became locked away in which type of rock?
questions.explain: Carbon became locked in sedimentary rocks like limestone and in fossil fuels.

questions.q: Incomplete combustion of fuels can produce which toxic gas?
questions.explain: Carbon monoxide is a toxic gas produced by incomplete combustion when oxygen is limited.

questions.q: Which human activity increases the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere?
questions.explain: Burning fossil fuels releases carbon dioxide, adding to atmospheric levels.

questions.q: What process caused the amount of oxygen in the atmosphere to increase?
questions.explain: Algae and plants increased oxygen levels through photosynthesis.

questions.q: Reducing, reusing and recycling materials is important because it:
options: Conserves finite resources and limited energy
questions.explain: Recycling conserves finite resources and uses less energy than making materials from scratch.

questions.q: Particulates released from burning fuels can cause:
questions.explain: Particulates cause global dimming and can damage health by causing respiratory problems.

questions.q: Acid rain damages the environment by:
options: Killing trees and aquatic life and eroding stonework
questions.explain: Acid rain harms trees, fish and lakes and corrodes buildings made of limestone.

questions.q: The first stage of treating fresh water to make it potable is usually:
questions.explain: Water is first filtered through filter beds to remove insoluble solids before sterilisation.

questions.q: The early atmosphere is thought to have been mainly which gas, released by volcanoes?
questions.explain: Volcanic activity released large amounts of carbon dioxide into the early atmosphere.

questions.q: Which oxides of nitrogen are mainly formed when fuels burn at the high temperatures inside engines?
options: From nitrogen and oxygen in the air reacting
From the carbon in the fuel
questions.explain: At high engine temperatures, nitrogen and oxygen from the air react to form oxides of nitrogen.

questions.q: A possible consequence of climate change caused by rising greenhouse gases is:
questions.explain: Increased greenhouse gases raise global temperatures, leading to more extreme weather.

questions.q: Which of these is the main greenhouse gas released by burning fossil fuels?
questions.explain: Burning fossil fuels releases carbon dioxide, the main greenhouse gas from this activity.

questions.q: In treating potable water from fresh sources, sterilisation is used to:
questions.explain: Sterilisation, for example with chlorine, kills harmful microbes in drinking water.

questions.q: What is meant by the carbon footprint of a product?
options: The total greenhouse gases emitted over its life cycle
The amount of carbon it contains only
questions.explain: A carbon footprint is the total amount of greenhouse gases emitted over the full life cycle of a product or service.

questions.q: Sulfur dioxide released from burning fuels causes which environmental problem?
questions.explain: Sulfur dioxide dissolves in rain water to form acid rain.

questions.q: Why is carbon monoxide especially dangerous to humans?
options: It is colourless and odourless and reduces oxygen carried by the blood
questions.explain: Carbon monoxide is toxic because it is hard to detect and stops blood carrying oxygen.

questions.q: What is the approximate composition of clean dry air today?
questions.explain: Today's air is about 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen, with small amounts of other gases.

questions.q: Why are fossil fuels described as finite resources?
options: They are being used up faster than they form
They form much faster than we use them
questions.explain: Fossil fuels take millions of years to form, so they are finite and being used up faster than they are replaced.

questions.q: Oxides of nitrogen formed in car engines contribute to:
questions.explain: Oxides of nitrogen contribute to acid rain and cause respiratory problems.

questions.q: Sea water can be made potable by distillation, but this method is costly because it:
questions.explain: Distillation requires a lot of energy to boil and condense the water, making it expensive.

specSource: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry (0620) syllabus; Chemistry Of The Environment
